t:
(a) 
Retroactive compensation or salary shall be paid by reason of this Act only in the case of an individual in the service of the United States (including service in the Armed Forces of the United States) or the municipal government of the District of Columbia on the date of enactment of this Act, except that such retroactive compensation or salary shall be paid (1) to an officer or employee who retired during the period beginning on the first day of the first pay period which begins on or after July 1, 1966, and ending on the date of enactment of this Act for services rendered during such period and (2) in accordance with the provisions of the Act of August 3, 1950 (Public Law 636, Eighty-first Congress), as amended (5 U.S.C. 61f–61k), for services rendered during the period beginning on the first day of the first pay period which begins on or after July 1, 1966, and ending on the date of enactment of this Act by an officer or employee who dies during such period. Such retroactive compensation or salary shall not be considered as basic salary for the purpose of the Civil Service Retirement Act in the case of any such retired or deceased officer or employee.
 
    (b) 
For the purposes of this section, service in the Armed Forces of the United States, in the case of an individual relieved from train-ing and service in the Armed Forces of the United States or discharged from hospitalization following such training and service, shall include the period provided by law for the mandatory restoration of such individual to a position in or under the Federal Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia.
 
    (c) 
For the purpose of determining the amount of insurance for which an individual is eligible under the Federal Employees’ Group Life Insurance Act of 1954, all changes in rates of compensation or salary which result from the enactment of this Act shall be held and considered to be effective as of the date of such enactment.

fable.w: This section only sets out who receives retroactive compensation under the Act and how it is treated for retirement and life insurance purposes. The one tempting hook is the mention of the municipal government of the District of Columbia, but it appears only as an employer whose staff are covered, not as a party consulted on any federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, rulemaking or right to sue.

qwen_block.w: This section defines eligibility for retroactive pay and insurance benefits for federal employees and District of Columbia municipal employees. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government in a decision-making process. The actors involved are federal employees and the government itself, which falls under the 'inside the federal government' exclusion.
qwen_block.s: Retroactive compensation or salary shall be paid by reason of this Act only in the case of an individual in the service of the United States (including service in the Armed Forces of the United States) or the municipal government of the District of Columbia on the date of enactment of this Act

opus.w: The section only sets eligibility rules for retroactive compensation and says how pay changes are treated for retirement and life insurance purposes. No outside party is consulted, coordinated with, or given a hearing or a right to sue. The District of Columbia government is mentioned only to say whose employees qualify for pay, not as a participant in any federal decision.
opus.b: This is a "No." Someone might be drawn to the words "individual in the service of the United States" or to the mention of the District of Columbia municipal government as an outside party. Neither holds up. The section only sets out who gets retroactive pay and how pay changes are treated for retirement and life insurance. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, no hearing or comment period is required, and no rulemaking is involved.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines eligibility for retroactive compensation for federal and D.C. government employees. It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties (such as the general public, states, or private entities) before making a decision. The individuals mentioned are government employees, who are considered inside the government for the purpose of this definition, and the text describes a benefit calculation rather than a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: Retroactive compensation or salary shall be paid by reason of this Act only in the case of an individual in the service of the United States (including service in the Armed Forces of the United States) or the municipal government of the District of Columbia on the date of enactment of this Act
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the statute affects "individuals in the service of the United States" and "municipal government of the District of Columbia," it involves outside parties. However, these individuals are federal or local government employees, and the statute merely defines their compensation eligibility. There is no requirement for the government to consult with these employees or any other outside group before making a decision; it is a unilateral determination of benefits.
